title: Witness statements (Valerie Thomas, Lisa Walker, Nurse A, Dr Pek Wan Lee)

blocks.text: 6 December 2022
Baby G
CONTENTS
Witness statement of VALERIE THOMAS (read)
Witness statement of LISA WALKER (read)
Witness statement of [NURSE A] (read)
Witness statement of DR PEK WAN LEE (read)
Second witness statement of DR PEK WAN LEE (read)
Tuesday, 6 December 2022
(In the absence of the jury)
My Lord should have a bundle of the witness statements (overspeaking) set out.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: I was helpfully reminded there's another witness statement at the back of the last bundle my Lord had that we hadn't reached, Valerie Thomas, so I'll do that one first. It's page 29.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: I don't have that bundle in front of me, but never mind, I'll listen and I'll then put it with these. Thank you.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: (In the presence of the jury)
Mr Astbury.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Witness statement of VALERIE THOMAS (read)
Thank you, my Lord. There are four witness statements to read with my Lord's leave, please.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: The first being from a witness by the name of Valerie Thomas. Her statement is signed on 19 March 2020. She says as follows:
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "In 2015 I was a full-time nursery nurse on the NNU at the Countess of Chester Hospital, predominantly working in special care rooms 3 and 4 within the NNU.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "The babies within 3 and 4 are described as stable babies, not on ventilation, starting to begin to feed, which we describe as feeding and growing. At a certain point babies within 3, mainly 4, get to the point that they are fit enough that they are allowed to go home.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "I have no recollection of [Baby G] or her parents.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: I will have to refer to the medical notes.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "In referring to the 7 September 2015 episode I have reviewed my medical notes and rotas from 1 September.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: I was working a night shift, 19.30 to 08.00 hours of 3 September going into 4 September. I don't remember looking after [Baby G] prior to 3 September.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "My first entry on the medical notes that relate to [Baby G] is timed at 06.16 on 4 September. The notes do not say which nursery room [Baby G] was in. [Baby G] was stable, being nursed in nasal-pronged oxygen as she had occasional desaturations, mainly after feeds. However, they were all self-correcting, which means there was no input for stimulation or to alter her oxygen levels, she automatically came back to normal herself.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "[Baby G] was offered an alternate bottle and nasogastric tube to which we were adding Gaviscon and fortifier to. We were starting to offer bottles to [Baby G] at that stage. However, [Baby G] did not complete any bottles for me that night.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "She passed urine and her bowels had opened, and medication was given as prescribed by two members of trained staff. As a nursery nurse I am not trained staff and all I could give medication-wise was vitamins and paracetamol, which would be checked by trained staff.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "The next entry by me on [Baby G]'s notes was timed at 05.59 on 5 September 2015. I was working the same night shift as 3 September. [Baby G] was classed as stable again and was in nasal-pronged oxygen. She was still having the occasional desaturations after feeding, all self-correcting. She was still being offered a bottle and nasogastric tube. At 5 am [Baby G] did manage to complete a full bottle. [Baby G] was still having Gaviscon and fortifier. She passed urine and had her bowels open. Her medication was given as prescribed. [Baby G]'s father was on the unit at 20.15 that night. [Baby G] I would describe as quite well."
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: My Lord, that concludes that statement.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: Witness statement of LISA WALKER (read)
Next, please, the statement of Lisa Walker.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: This statement is dated 13 September 2018. The jury will recall, I'm sure, Lisa Walker, one of the neonatal nursery nurses from whom we've already heard, as in fact was Valerie Thomas, who I have just read. I should have probably said in advance, I'm sorry.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: I think the name will have rung a bell.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Yes. Lisa Walker in this statement says as follows:
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "I have been specifically asked into the care of [Baby G] [as read]..."
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: She gives [Baby G]'s date of birth at 31 May 2015:
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "... on 7 September 2015. I have had the opportunity to view nurses' notes relating to [Baby G] to which I may refer.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "With regard to 7 September 2015, referring to my notes, between the 6th and the 7th, I was a night shift, 19.30 to 08.00 hours with [Nurse E], Lucy Letby, Christopher Booth and Ailsa Simpson.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "The staffing levels were fine for that night shift and everything was as normal. [Nurse E] was the designated nurse for [Baby G] that night. After the initial handover that evening I was allocated the care of two stable babies that were in special care nurseries 3 and 4 within the NNU.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "I do have access to all four nurseries and there is no restriction of movement. However, my babies would mainly be in nurseries 3 and 4. If the ward is quiet, nursery 4 could be closed and I could be in nursery 2 and 3 looking after my designated babies. I cannot remember how many babies were on the ward that night.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: If there is an emergency we, as nursing assistants, will step up and make sure all the other babies in any of the nurseries are looked after while the emergency is in progress.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "From the nursing notes [Nurse E] went for a break.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: Shortly after [Baby G] had a large vomit. [Baby G] had a full abdomen and was straining. After [Baby G] had vomited she had an apnoeic episode dropping her saturation levels.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: Somebody must have called the doctor. Dr Ventress arrived within minutes. [Baby G] was taken into nursery 1 and had to be vented
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: that night. [Baby G] went on to nil by mouth. She then went on to 10% dextrose as she wasn't feeding.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "From memory, [Baby G] was in nursery 2, in the far left corner as you enter the room. Leading up to [Nurse E] taking her break later that morning, I cannot remember what time she actually went, but I did not notice anyone going to nursery 2 prior to [Nurse E] taking that break.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: However, I can't say for sure.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "I do know that I did not go into nursery 2 prior to [Nurse E] taking her break. According to the notes, it was whilst [Nurse E] was on her break that [Baby G] had vomited.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: I cannot remember exactly what nursery I was in at this time but I would have been looking after another baby within nursery 3 or 4. I don't remember any alarm being sounded at the time of [Baby G]'s collapse. I can state that if I was in either nursery 3 or 4, I cannot see nurseries 1 and 2 from either one of them as my vision is blocked by walls. However, I would be able to hear any alarm activation in any of the four nurseries.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "I do remember being in a position to see at least Lucy, and possibly Ailsa, cleaning up the vomit around [Baby G]'s cot in nursery 2. Therefore I must have been, at some time, outside nursery 2 in the corridor. I cannot say for sure if I actually assisted with the cleaning up of the vomit but I don't think I did as I didn't see the vomit for myself. I do remember Lucy discussing with, I think, Ailsa that the vomit was everywhere around the cot within nursery 2.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "Obviously, someone had called for the doctor to attend. I cannot remember if it was me from instruction or whether it was somebody else. Dr Ventress did attend within minutes to care for [Baby G]. Dr Brearey, later on into the shift, did attend the unit. I cannot say where Christopher was during this event.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "I cannot remember how long it was before [Baby G] was moved to nursery 1 or who by. I cannot remember if I did go into nursery 1 from that point onwards.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: I believe, according to the notes, Lucy became the designated nurse once [Baby G] had entered nursery 1.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: I am not aware of any debrief that has taken place regarding the care of [Baby G]. I didn't see [Baby G]'s vomit, full abdomen or straining."
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: That concludes, my Lord, Lisa Walker's statement.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes, thank you very much.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Witness statement of [NURSE A] (read)
If we move on next, please, to [Nurse A], who again the jury will recall, I'm sure.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Her statement in this matter is dated 27 April 2018:
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "I am making this further statement to Chester Constabulary regarding the investigation concerning increased neonatal mortality at the Countess of Chester Hospital NHS Foundation Trust between June 2015 and July 2016.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "I have been informed this particular interview..."
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: Pausing there, my Lord, the jury will recall that some witnesses are interviewed in advance and then the statement prepared from that particular interview:
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "... is in reference to [Baby G], date of birth 31/5/2015. I have had the opportunity to view medical notes relevant to the dates that have been specified to me.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "With regard to 7 September 2015, from memory I remember this day in particular as [Baby G] was 100 days old. The NNU will celebrate this particular birthday as it is seen as a milestone. A member of staff will bake a cake and there will be balloons around the bedside of the baby concerned. I was working a day shift and I was the designated nurse for [Baby G] that day, who was in nursery 1 on a ventilator. I remember [Baby G] being very poorly that day, which surprised me and the staff as prior to 7 September [Baby G] was stable and in one of the outside nurseries.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "I remember giving [Baby G] various medicines throughout the day and I was aware that [Baby G] was going to be transferred back to Arrowe Park Hospital. I have looked after [Baby G] before in the past. I couldn't say how many times but essentially she was what we call 'feeding and growing' on these occasions. I cannot remember if I was working the day before on 6 September.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "Referring from the notes and memory, [Baby G] was born at Arrowe Park Hospital and then transferred to the Countess of Chester Hospital NNU. I was working a 07.30 to 20.00 hours shift. I can't remember who I was working with. I was the designated nurse for [Baby G] on that day and only [Baby G] was in nursery 1.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "When I first came on duty, and during the verbal handover process from Nurse Lucy Letby, Lucy told me that [Baby G] had vomited whilst under the care of [Nurse E] and then became unwell. Lucy told me that she had taken over as designated nurse from [Nurse E] for [Baby G] as [Nurse E] did not have her intensive care course qualification, which was required to care for [Baby G] during the remaining (sic) of that shift.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "From the notes there were blood pressure issues all day with [Baby G]. From the notes, [Baby G] had vomited a large projectile vomit and Dr Ventress was asked to review [Baby G]. [Baby G] was reviewed by Dr Ventress and put on nil by mouth. Dr Ventress was then called away to theatre to another baby. In the meantime [Baby G] had become apnoeic and it was later on that [Baby G] was intubated and put on a ventilator.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "I would have checked all of [Baby G]'s requirements, checking what fluids and medication she was on. If I remember rightly, her CRP was raised; this would indicate infection."
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: My Lord, pausing there, this witness appears on the sequence of events chart on a number of occasions, so I'm going to summarise those entries she's made for the assistance of the jury.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: Mr Murphy, if we could go, please, to tile 134, first. And if we can go behind it -- sorry, 135, I do apologise. If we can go behind it, please.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: Ladies and gentlemen, if we look, please, initially at this document and knowing that [Nurse A] came on at 07.00 hours on the 7th and recognising perhaps, as far as we can, previous documents she's endorsed, we can see her signatures down the right-hand side of the form throughout the shift. Apart from one occasion, which I think is at 15.58, where it's a different signature, but in effect this is the blood gas record that she has completed through the shift.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: We can see the last entry there in the middle of the page at 8.07. So that's the first document that's relevant and in the sequence of events. We can go next, with a bit more confidence, to 141, please. If we look at the chart.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: To the right-hand side we can see a row of initials which appear to indicate [initials of Nurse A], if we scroll up, consistent with the time when she was on duty.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: Reading from that particular column, from 08.00 onwards, we can see the entries that she has made in respect of heart rate, which we've heard from other witnesses before is clearly in excess of what would be expected in the circumstances.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: If we can scroll down, please, we can also see her entries in respect of respirations and temperature.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: Other entries that we're all becoming familiar with lower down the page. But that's where to find that document if anybody needs to see it.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: My Lord, I'm only going to refer to it once, like a number of documents, because the same document appears on the hour over and over again, so I'm not going to refer to it again for the purposes of this exercise. So they are her entries on the observations chart.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: I'm reminded there are also hard copies of this particular document in the files, as there are most of these core documents. We'll go through them now if we may just to remind the jury where to look if they need to on the system.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: Tile 142 next, please. This is headed "Environmental safety check form". It's in a different format than we've become used to with other babies. If we look to the bottom, we see across the bottom signatures or initials "[Nurse A]". Thank you.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: If we scroll up, Mr Murphy, we can see, by comparison to the times, a number of entries from 08.00 hours across until 19.00 hours with the various measurements and readings that [Nurse A] entered on that particular form. So any queries with regards to that can be accessed via tile 142.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: Next tile, please, 143. If we can look at that.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: Dated 7 September. This is a midnight to midnight form, of course, so we can scroll down a little bit, please.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: Pausing there, Mr Murphy, we can see at 4 am the commencement of the glucose with [Baby G] having gone nil by mouth after the vomiting.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: We can then see in the bolus column, various boluses through the course of the 24-hour period. Again if we look to the right -scroll down a little bit further, please -- we can see those initials [Nurse A] on each and every occasion on the hour, relevant endorsements in respect of fluids.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: Moving on next, please -- I should say her entries are all between 08.00 and 19.00 on that particular form.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: Tile 144 next, please. This is the intravenous and subcutaneous infusion prescription chart on 7 September.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: The second entry is made at 08.20 hours and appears to have [Nurse A] in the initials. Certainly it may be that the entry at 15.20 is the same. I'm not going to speculate about others, but that reflects those infusions that were given during the course of the shift that [Nurse A] is recounting.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: We can go next, please, to tile 145. Similar information represented in a slightly different format.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: Again, it illustrates the provision of various infusions through the date during the shift of [Nurse A]. So that tile, if any queries arise in that regard.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: Could we go next, please, to tile 170. No need to go behind this one, I don't think. It simply indicates the administration of what we've learned is an antibiotic at 12.50 in the afternoon, together with Nurse Williamson as she is now known.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: I am not going to repeat all of those charts again through the course of the shift, but if we could go next, please, to tile 284, and look at that form, please, Mr Murphy.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: You can see the continuation of the observation chart follows on from the one we looked at earlier, with [Nurse A] making the first four entries according to the signatures. If we can just scroll up again, that will accord, I suspect, with the times in the top box: 17.00, 18.00, 19.00 and 20.00.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: No, no, first three entries. If you look at the initials at the bottom -- I'm looking at the paper copy we have --
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: -- I think the fourth one is BS, Belinda Simcock.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Nurse Williamson, yes. Difficult to keep up.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: I've been following which ones with got in paper. Some of these that have been referred to, you've got the paper copies, others you haven't. This one, you do have the paper copy in section 7 of file 2.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Thank you.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: So that's both of the observation charts covered.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: If we can look next, please, at 287. It's a new fluid balance chart.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: That commences with what appears to be an infusion of dobutamine, commenced at 17.00. We have an entry of nil by mouth on the left-hand column. It looks to me like certainly two of the signatures on the right, not three, are those of [Nurse A] and it would be consistent with the times in the left-hand box, which is 17.00, 18.00 and 19.00 hours respectively.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: Finally, please, in respect of charts, tile 289.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: A form we saw particularly in the case of [Baby F], a prescription for Babiven Maintenance, TPN as we've been calling it. That was first hung at 17.10 on 7 September.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: Returning now, please, if I may, to the witness statement, my Lord:
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "From my notes [says [Nurse A]] I remember [Baby G]'s physical condition as peripheral, ie cool on the edges, hands and feet, and [Baby G] was pale too. [Baby G] had several infusions to support her blood pressure. She had cannulas put in with a long line inserted. In my nursing notes with regards to medication that day, [Baby G] had four saline boluses, we increased the quantity of antibiotic cefotaxime to 50 milligrams per kilogram.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: [Baby G] was also on inotropes, dopamine and dobutamine.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: My notes are timed at 20.50 that evening, therefore obviously I have remained on duty for whatever reason I cannot remember."
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: Then if we go to those notes now, please, 319 is the first tile. [Nurse A] has entered "08.00 until present":
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "During handover required x2 episodes of Neopuff.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: All fluids and lines checked with L Letby. Correct and lines patent. Ventilation increased to 26/6 as responded to higher pressures on Neopuff. CBG showed over-ventilation so pressure and rate reduced as charted.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "NiBP dropped around 08.00 and dopamine commenced peripherally as no long line at time. Blood pressure improved slightly and inotrope titrated as prescribed.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: BP [we'll assume that is blood pressure seeing as that's the entry in the statement] deteriorated and cannula site became white. Moved to another cannula. BP again improved. Doctors trying to obtain long line for better access. Second cannula tissued and for a short time no dopamine running until long line available. Long line obtained and dopamine and Maintenance transferred to it.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: Midaz and morph continued to run peripherally. Further cannula obtained for bolus and [antibiotics]. Chest clear and CBG/ABG [arterial the latter I assume] continue to be metabolic acidosis x4. Sodium chloride 0.9% bolus given as prescribed. Cef increased to 50mg/kg and given as prescribed. Initially pyrexial.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: Now normothermic but periph cold. Perfusion has remained poor all day."
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: Sorry, I think you read it -- sorry, you read... Just go back to that.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Of course.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: The last paragraph:
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: "Chest clear and [capillary blood gases] and [arterial blood gases] continue to be metabolic acidosis."
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Then a full stop:
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: "Times four sodium chloride 0.9% bolus given as prescribed."
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Ah, I have got my "times four" in the wrong place.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: Exactly. It was four boluses of sodium chloride.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Thank you.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: Sorry about that, but it's just the way you read it.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: My mistake. If we can go to the next note, please. Tile 320. Timed at 20.12:
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "Discussed with pharmacy. Dopamine, dobutamine and adrenaline can [I think that should be 'all'] run via same long line if required if no other alternative available. No ETT or oral suction required all day.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: Minimal urine output all day. Blood plus 1, protein plus 1. Catheter in situ..."
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: And I think we all know now that's bowels not opened.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: 322, please. This is the parental communication update, made at 20.51:
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "Parents on unit throughout day and updated. Aware that blood pressure is too low and IV access difficult.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: Understandable very upset and struggling to see her this poorly again. Have looked at 100 day cake, are trying to remain positive at this stage. Are staying tonight and have currently gone home to get supplies. [Dr C] will update in full detail when they return."
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: Finally, please, tile 323. This is the final note made on the shift at 20.54:
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "Capillary blood gas continued to deteriorate despite increasing inotropes. Colour and perfusion deteriorating. Doctors present at the time of handover."
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: My Lord, again, just concluding the statement now:
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "From the notes, I handed over to Belinda Simcock.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: The parents of [Baby G] were on the NNU most of the day until returning home to get provisions just before handover at the end of my shift. Referring from the doctors' notes, there are entries of [Baby G] being transferred to Arrowe Park Hospital.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "My opinion of [Baby G]'s condition was sepsis or possibly something that we call NEC, which is an infection of the bowel. I would describe the parents as a lovely, caring couple who were committed to [Baby G].
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: They were very competent when doing things for [Baby G]."
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: My Lord, that concludes [Nurse A]’s statement.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: Witness statement of DR PEK WAN LEE (read)

We move on in the timeline at this stage to Dr Lee. In his statement, his first statement on 28 August 2019, he heads his statement with [Baby G]'s name and the admission period of the 8th to 16 September 2015. It says as follows:
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "I am Dr Pek Wan Lee, neonatal consultant at Wirral University Teaching Hospital since March 2011. I have been a consultant since March 2001. I was the named consultant for [Baby G] for this admission. I looked after her from the 8th to 10 September 2015 as I was the service week consultant, and the following service week consultant looked after her until her discharge back to the Countess of Chester NNU.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "[Baby G] was born at the Wirral University Teaching Hospital on 31 May 2015 at 23 plus 6 weeks. Birth weight was 535 grams. She
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: was an in utero transfer from the Countess of Chester Hospital and therefore was discharged with a diagnosis of chronic lung disease of prematurity to the Countess of Chester NNU on 13 August 2015 when her need for tertiary level neonatal care was over.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "Following a respiratory deterioration due to presumed sepsis at the Countess of Chester Hospital NNU on 7 September 2015, she was transferred to our NNU on 8 September 2015 at 04.30 hours when she was 100 days old. Her weight on admission was 1,985 grams and temperature 36.8 degrees Celsius.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "She required ventilatory support with 100% oxygen on her first day, which was then gradually weaned. Her sedation on admission was with morphine and midazolam.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: She was extubated on 13 September 2015 to nasal cannula oxygen before self-ventilating in air from 15 September 2015.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "She had severe hypertension, requiring support with fluid boluses and inotropic medications of dopamine, dobutamine, adrenaline, noradrenaline and hydrocortisone. These medications were gradually reduced and finally discontinued on 12 September 2015.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: She also had metabolic acidosis, which required bicarbonate correction.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "She had jittery movements at times which were never treated with anti-convulsants and later resolved. She underwent an MRI brain scan on 15 September 2015, which was reported as a difficult scan to interpret due to movement with resulting limitations.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "The appearances were suggestive of a significant hypoxic or ischaemic insult, abnormality in both cerebellar hemispheres, possibly established infarcts.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: A second opinion from Alder Hey Children's Hospital was advised as well as a repeat scan in a couple of months.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: Her retinopathy screen showed grade 1 retinopathy of prematurity.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "[Baby G] required a blood transfusion on 9 September 2015 for anaemia. She was also given additional vitamin K doses for 48 hours as her coagulation was mildly deranged and there was bloodstaining of her endotracheal aspirates.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "Due to significant oedema her fluids were restricted initially to 100ml per kilogram of 10% glucose with sodium and potassium supplementation.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: Fluids were gradually liberalised as her clinical condition improved. She was catheterised for monitoring of her urine input as initially it was very poor. It then gradually improved and there were no long-lasting concerns with her renal function.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "She was nil orally on being transferred and gradual feeding was introduced as her condition stabilised.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: There were transient abdominal concerns on the 12th to 13 September 2015 and her abdominal X-ray was discussed with the Alder Hey consultant paediatric surgeon who thought it was likely to be ileus related to sepsis.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: She was able to tolerate steadily increasing feeds after that. She received oral sodium and phosphate supplementation.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "Her triple antibiotic therapy, which was commenced in Chester, was changed to monotherapy with meropenem.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: Blood, cerebrospinal fluid, respiratory and urine cultures were all negative. Her respiratory viral screen was also negative. However, her C-reactive protein, CPR, which is an infection marker, was 150 milligrams per litre on admission, rose to 218 milligrams per litre on 9 September, before gradually coming down to 11 milligrams per litre by the 16th. She completed a seven-day course of meropenem.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "Her parents were updated on a regular basis. She was discharged to the Countess of Chester on 16 September 2015 at 15.00 hours with a weight of 2,095 grams, head circumference 30.5 centimetres. She was self-ventilating in air and continued to establish her enteral feeds.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "In summary, [Baby G]'s readmission on the 8th to 16 September was for presumed sepsis leading to multi-organ dysfunction requiring intensive support.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: She was very unwell on arrival and gradually improved to not needing any support on discharge except to fully establish enteral feeding.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "The presumption of sepsis was based on her clinical picture and markedly elevated CRP (normal is less than 5) as her cultures were all negative."
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: He then states that the statement is accurate within the best of his knowledge and belief.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: My Lord, there's a second statement from Dr Lee.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes. Wirral University Teaching Hospital is Arrowe Park?
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: It is.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: Just in case you were wondering. As we know, [Baby G] came from Arrowe Park and then went back and went back again to the Countess of Chester. And there were quite a lot of medical terms in there in relation to hypoxia and that sort of thing. Hypoxia is essentially starvation of oxygen to whatever tissue it is, so if it's to the brain then it's an hypoxic brain injury.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: I think hypoxia is covered in the glossary.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: It is, I have just checked, and it does say:
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: "Hypoxia: a condition in which the body is deprived of adequate oxygen supply at the tissue level. Hypoxic due to insufficient oxygenation. Hypoxic ischaemic encephalopathy [he doesn't actually refer to the encephalopathy in that statement], a brain injury condition caused by oxygen deprivation to the brain."
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: There is reference to the cerebral hemispheres of the brain.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Thank you, my Lord. We will be hearing from an expert with regard to those particular aspects.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: Exactly. It's just there was a lot of medical information in that statement.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Second witness statement of DR PEK WAN LEE (read)
There's a second statement with that in mind from Dr Lee, who on 4 June 2020 provided a further statement which reads as follows:
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "I would like to add that [Baby G] did not collapse on the 12th and 13 September 2015. She was fully weaned off her inotropic support on 12 September and extubated to nasal cannula oxygen on the 13th. Both these events are in keeping with an increasingly stable patient.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "[Baby G] had an abdominal X-ray on 12 September 2015 as there was a concern that her abdomen looked distended, not because of a collapse. The abdominal X-ray was reviewed by the Alder Hey surgeons and they were not concerned. They thought they might
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: have had ileus due to sepsis. This clinical concern lessened as she was able to tolerate increasing feeds.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "[Baby G] was transferred back to the Countess of Chester Hospital on 16 September 2015 because she was no longer needing intensive care support in a tertiary neonatal unit. [Baby G] was self-ventilating in air and continuing to establish enteral feeding. We were not concerned about her presumed sepsis status by then as her CRP had fallen steadily to a nearly normal level of 11 milligrams per litre [repeating there that normal is less than 5] from a peak of 218 milligrams per litre and all her cultures had returned negative. As [Baby G] was clinically stable, the Countess of Chester Hospital would be able to continue her care in their neonatal unit. We were following the neonatal network policy of transferring babies back to their referring hospitals after their need for tertiary neonatal care was over.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "[Baby G], on transfer to the Countess of Chester Hospital on 16 September 2015, was clear of sepsis as she was clinically stable with decreasing CRP and negative cultures.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "We would use the clinical picture, culture results, the CRP level and the full blood count to help diagnose sepsis. All of these were reassuring at the time we transferred [Baby G] back to Chester."
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: That concludes that second statement, my Lord.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes. Thank you very much.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS
